title: Exotic magnetism and persistent spin dynamics in a frustrated Jeff = 1/2 triangular lattice antiferromagnet
authors: M. Barman, K. Jaksetič, M. Pregelj, M. D. Le. P. J. Baker, A. Zorko, P. Khuntia
abstract: The delicate interplay between competing degrees of freedom, anisotropy, and frustration-induced strong quantum fluctuations in pseudospin-$J_{\rm eff}=1/2$ rare-earth triangular-lattice antiferromagnets offers a promising platform for the experimental realization of exotic states with nontrivial low-energy excitations. Here, we present thermodynamic, inelastic neutron scattering (INS), and muon spin relaxation ($μ$SR) investigations of the frustrated magnet K$_3$NdTe$_2$O$9$, in which Nd$^{3+}$ ions constitute a structurally perfect triangular lattice with no detectable site disorder. The experiments reveal the realization of a Kramers doublet ground state with $J{\rm eff}=1/2$ moments, well separated from the first excited state, which interact antiferromagnetically with an exchange interaction of $\sim$0.6 K between the Nd$^{3+}$ moments in the triangular plane. The absence of oscillations and the so-called 1/3 plateau in the zero-field $μ$SR asymmetry down to 50 mK rules out long-range magnetic ordering and spin freezing on the $μ$SR time scale, respectively. The temperature dependence of the zero-field $μ$SR relaxation rate is well described by the Orbach relaxation mechanism, indicating the existence of fluctuating moments in the ground state of this frustrated magnet. Our results demonstrate exotic magnetism and persistent spin dynamics down to 50 mK. These observations establish this new family of frustrated rare-earth triangular-lattice antiferromagnets as a promising venue for the experimental realization of nontrivial quantum states with exotic low-energy excitations.
summary: This work investigates the exotic magnetism of $	ext{K}_3	ext{NdTe}_2	ext{O}_9$, a geometrically frustrated triangular lattice antiferromagnet. By combining $\mu	ext{SR}$, specific heat, and INS measurements, the authors confirm that the system enters a dynamic ground state characterized by $J_{	ext{eff}}=1/2$ moments. The results strongly support persistent spin dynamics rather than conventional long-range magnetic ordering down to very low temperatures.
main_problem: To investigate exotic magnetism and persistent spin dynamics in a geometrically frustrated rare-earth triangular-lattice antiferromagnet.
main_result: The experiments rule out long-range magnetic ordering down to 50 mK, confirming the existence of a fluctuating ground state characterized by $	ext{J}_{	ext{eff}}=1/2$ moments and persistent spin dynamics.
method: A combination of thermodynamic measurements (Specific Heat), inelastic neutron scattering ($	ext{INS}$), muon spin relaxation ($\mu	ext{SR}$), and magnetization studies were employed.
model_or_system: The system is the frustrated magnet $	ext{K}_3	ext{NdTe}_2	ext{O}_9$, where $	ext{Nd}^{3+}$ ions form a structurally perfect triangular lattice. The low-energy physics is modeled by effective $J_{	ext{eff}}=1/2$ moments interacting via strong exchange interactions.
key_observables: Zero-field $\mu	ext{SR}$ asymmetry (showing no oscillations or 1/3 plateau), temperature dependence of the $\mu	ext{SR}$ relaxation rate ($\lambda$), and specific heat anomalies.
important_parameters: Exchange interaction strength ($J_{	ext{ex}}/k_B \sim 0.6 	ext{ K}$); low temperatures down to $50 	ext{ mK}$; effective spin quantum number $	ext{J}_{	ext{eff}}=1/2$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the Orbach relaxation mechanism describes the temperature dependence of the $\mu	ext{SR}$ rate, and that dipolar interactions are negligible compared to exchange interactions.
figures_summary: Figures show $\mu	ext{SR}$ asymmetry spectra (zero-field and applied field) demonstrating persistent dynamics; plots illustrate the thermally activated behavior of the relaxation rate ($\lambda$) vs. temperature.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents evidence from multiple techniques: structural characterization, magnetic susceptibility/magnetization to establish $	ext{J}_{	ext{eff}}=1/2$ ground state and weak exchange coupling; then uses $\mu	ext{SR}$ and specific heat measurements to confirm the absence of static order and characterize the low-energy spin dynamics.
why_interesting: The study provides experimental evidence for quantum disordered magnetic states (approaching QSL behavior) in a real material system, which is highly relevant to understanding frustrated magnetism and exotic ground states that can be modeled using advanced many-body techniques.

FIG. 2. Inelastic neutron scattering (INS) intensity at 5K for the incident neutron energies of 180, 60, 29.7 and 2 meV. Besides the broad diffuse phonon excitations at larger scattering vectors Q, there are clear additional flat bands at low Q that correspond to CEF levels. Furthermore, the flat bands at E > 60 meV which have maximal intensity at ∼7 meV, most likely correspond to molecular vibrations from adsorbed water. For clarity, we also show the energy transfer integrated across the low Q range to emphasize the flat bands. The red lines are Gaussian fits, performed to precisely determined the energies of the CEF excitations.
